root_cause.text: Using sizeof() on an array of pointers (snor_f_names) in spi_nor_params_show() passed the total byte size instead of the element count to spi_nor_print_flags(), causing an out-of-bounds read due to an inflated bounds check.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states that "sizeof(snor_f_names) returns the total number of bytes occupied by the pointers (element_count * sizeof(void *)) rather than the element count itself," and "An out-of-bounds read occurs if a flag bit is set that exceeds the array's actual element count but is within the inflated byte-size count." The patch replaces sizeof() with ARRAY_SIZE().

intent_record.intent_summary: Add explicit include for array_size.h to guarantee availability of ARRAY_SIZE macro.
intent_record.what: Added #include <linux/array_size.h> to the list of includes in the source file.
intent_record.how: This ensures that the ARRAY_SIZE macro (or similar definitions) is explicitly available, preventing potential implicit dependency issues and making the code more robust against header reorganisation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix flag name array size passed to spi_nor_print_flags to use ARRAY_SIZE instead of sizeof to correctly count elements.
intent_record.what: Replaced sizeof(snor_f_names) with ARRAY_SIZE(snor_f_names) in the call to spi_nor_print_flags.
intent_record.how: The change ensures that the correct number of elements (array size) is passed instead of the total byte size of the array, preventing potential out-of-bounds access or incorrect behavior when iterating over the flag names.
